newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-S.A. CRICKETERS TO BE PAID FOR PERFORMANCE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-S.A. CRICKETERS TO BE PAID FOR PERFORMANCE.

text.p: South Africa's cricketers stand to earn rich pickings next summer, as long as they perform successfully, the United Cricket Board of South Africa (UCBSA) announced on Thursday.
The team could earn themselves a bonus of 500,000 rand ($111,000) if they win any of the test series against Pakistan and Australia next season, UCBSA managing director Ali Bacher told Reuters.
South Africa are set to play 11 test matches, both at home and abroad, during the 1997-98 summer against Pakistan, Australia and Sri Lanka.

Test series wins against both Pakistan (away and home) and Australia (away) would benefit South Africa by 500,000 rand each while victory in the two-test series against Sri Lanka at home next March would give them 350,000 rand, Bacher said.
Bacher said South Africa would earn a team bonus of 200,000 rand for drawing the test series against both Pakistan and Australia and 135,000 rand for drawing with Sri Lanka.
"It's more performance-oriented than last year," Bacher said. "Last season, we won four tests, lost four tests and drew one - and that was perceived as an ordinary summer for us.
"This coming season our philosophy is that, the better the team does, the better we will do overall - there will be bigger crowds, more sponsorship and therefore more money for development."

South Africa's domestic cricket fixtures were also announced for 1997-98 , a busy season which begins on October 1 and finishes on April 23 with the reserve day for the triangular series involving South Africa, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.
